column2: Act Ten
Seven Deadly Sins

I've already admitted I'm a loser, so let me have an easy life, Lu Mingfei thought. Heroics aren't supposed to have anything to do with me. You know perfectly well I can't do anything, and still you make me watch something this sad, a girl I like slowly dying. All right, all right, I don't really like her that much. But I'm really scared she'll die.
And still there was nothing he could do... A loser couldn't do a thing!
“Don't die!” he shouted with all his strength. Without realizing it, he felt tears roll down his cheeks.

The world was so lonely. Eighty meters underwater, you were as alone as if you stood on a planet by yourself. No one could hear you speak. You could scream at the top of your lungs, and no one would care.
Lu Mingfei and Nono struggled through the torrent at full speed.

Every passage and chamber they passed through was changing. Enormous bronze mechanisms scraped against one another with a clacking sound. Massive gates, towering bronze walls, huge gears and thick shafts moved around them. They were like two tiny fish thrown into a gigantic machine.
“Wait ahead for one minute. One minute. A passage will open on your right in one minute.”
“Pick up speed. The exit ahead will disappear in twenty seconds.”
“Turn left. Avoid the gate ahead!”

Norma's commands came from college headquarters half a world away. With the map in hand, the supercomputer worked with astonishing efficiency; every instruction was clear and precise. One mistake, and Lu Mingfei and Nono could be crushed flat.
“You are approaching the bottom of the bronze city. You'll find an exit there, but in thirty seconds the city will lock completely!” Norma said.
“Where's the exit?” Lu Mingfei looked around.
Bronze walls surrounded them. They were in a square chamber filled with water, and the passage through which they had entered was already sealed. The walls rumbled and shook.
“There.” Nono pointed a short distance away, her voice strange.
Lu Mingfei followed the beam of his lamp and shuddered violently. His hand tightened involuntarily around Nono's.
“Is that him?” he whispered.
“Yes, even though he's like this now.”

A hideous face protruded from the bronze wall directly below them. The living spirit had opened its mouth, exposing sharp bronze teeth clamped around a man's arm. The man was a skeleton now. Cassell College's specially made diving suit hung on his bones, drifting gently in the water. The lamp shone into his mask, revealing two dark eye sockets.
The identification tag around his neck bore his name: Ye Sheng, Cassell College Executive Department, Assistant Commissioner, No. 08203118.
They had found Ye Sheng. He had reached this place, but he had never left it.
“He used his own blood to open the door?” Lu Mingfei asked.

“To command a living spirit, you need an extremely pure dragon bloodline. The Key is one example; you're another. If your blood isn't pure enough... you can sacrifice a great quantity of it instead. The consequence is death from blood loss,” Nono said quietly. “There are records of people opening dragon secret palaces this way. The college's operations manual forbids it. Forcing a bloodline to work at the cost of a tremendous sacrifice... in the Middle Ages, techniques like that gave birth to black magic.”
“I see.” Lu Mingfei sighed softly.
They swam together to Ye Sheng's remains. Nono was silent for a moment, then reached out and gently touched the mask of his diving suit.
“He doesn't have an oxygen tank,” Lu Mingfei said.
“I saw.” Nono said, “That's why Aki managed to reach the surface even though there clearly wasn't enough oxygen. Ye Sheng gave her his tank, so she had twice as much.”
Lu Mingfei nodded. “He was really cool!”
“He always was,” Nono said softly.
“What's that behind him?”
Behind Ye Sheng, where his oxygen tank should have been, was a long case lashed tightly to his body. Lu Mingfei tapped it, and it gave a low metallic ring.
“They must have found it with the brass jar, but Aki couldn't carry it out alone. Whatever it is, let's take it,” Nono said. “I'll carry it.”
She untied the case from Ye Sheng and strapped it to herself.
“Lu Mingfei, Chen Motong, get out quickly! Get out quickly! Only twenty seconds left!” Norma's voice rang in their headsets.

Lu Mingfei suddenly sensed something wrong. He looked up and saw that his lamp beam no longer reached very far. Then he understood: it wasn't because the water had grown cloudy. Above them, an enormous bronze wall was descending silently, like a gigantic hydraulic press!
“Quick! Open the door!” Nono shouted.

Lu Mingfei squeezed his finger desperately, trying to force a drop of blood into the living spirit's mouth. Nothing came. His wrist had been bound and his hand had spent too long in the water; it was nearly as pale as a dead man's. He drew his diving knife, cut the whole glove off, and squeezed his finger with all his might. Only a few drops emerged. But his hand was shaking, and the drops dissolved into drifting threads as soon as they hit the water, never reaching the spirit's mouth.
The bronze wall overhead was little more than a meter above them. Neither he nor Nono could stand upright. In a few more seconds they would be crushed to pulp.
“Cut your finger open!” Nono shouted.
“R-right...” Lu Mingfei brought the knife to his finger.
He was cutting his own finger, after all, and had no confidence in the stroke. He slashed twice, leaving two small cuts, but still scarcely any blood came out.
Should he cut the other hand? But then he would have to bind that wrist to keep his oxygen from escaping, and he didn't have enough left to last much longer.
“Stay calm, stay calm, stay calm...” he muttered over and over. The hand holding the knife still shook.
“Don't be afraid!” Nono said.
“Don't be afraid, don't be afraid, don't be afraid...” Lu Mingfei tried to shift position, but the moment he straightened his back, his head struck the bronze wall overhead.

Less than a meter of space remained. The cramped chamber was suffocating, like lying in a coffin and looking up at its lid. Lu Mingfei shivered. His vision darkened, and the diving knife slipped from his hand.
“Hurry! Pick up the knife!” Nono kicked him.
Still so violent at a time like this? Kicking me? Lu Mingfei thought. We're about to die.

He lunged for the knife and glanced back at Nono. He froze. She was sitting on the floor, bracing the descending bronze wall with her head and both hands in a triangle. She could only kick him because her hands were occupied; if she moved them, her neck might be crushed. This girl was insane. How many more seconds could she hold it up? What were human bones against a giant hydraulic press? They'd crack and splinter in an instant.
“Hurry. Don't think about anything else. All we need is one drop of your blood.” Nono's voice was calm.
Did she have to be so moving? Acting like the big boss, as if holding it up would keep both of them alive. Lu Mingfei squeezed his finger hard, thoughts racing, almost hearing Nono's bones crack.

He remembered the old cartoon She-Ra: Princess of Power. Its heroine was a violent girl who only had to draw her sword and shout “Give me strength!” to transform, wearing a miniskirt and riding a winged white horse. Her slender arms held immense strength; even if a mountain fell on her, she could lift it.
But Nono wasn't She-Ra. She didn't even have a Yanling. The little witch was nearly at the end of her strength.
“Damn it, I'm doing it!” A sudden reckless impulse surged through Lu Mingfei.
Put simply, blood rushed to his head. That fury, that willingness to risk everything, had come over him again.
Those people didn't know, did they? They'd never cared what he thought, had they? Everyone thought he was a coward, right? But when the moment came, he could suddenly go crazy too!

He ripped away the tourniquet from his wrist. That deadly band was like the one a doctor tied around your arm when you donated blood: it held back his blood, and also held in the oxygen as precious as life itself underwater.
Blood rushed through his vessels to his fingertips. Countless bubbles poured from his diving suit, and icy water flooded Lu Mingfei's mouth.
Lu Mingfei slapped his hand hard against the living spirit's face, as though striking it across the mouth.

His oxygen pressure fell rapidly. High-pressure gas dissolved in his blood began to escape. Blood rushed to his brain, his vision went black, and his hands flailed for something that would make him feel safe. Amid the countless bubbles, someone held him tight.
Lu Mingfei's cry echoed through the Moniach's forward cabin. Manstein's body jerked, and he opened his eyes.
“Rescue... oxygen leak...” The last words were Nono's voice, coming from Manstein's mouth.
He had spent the last of his strength and fainted.
“Oxygen leak?” Caesar stared, then looked toward the river where they had anchored, about two kilometers away.
“Prepare the diving bell!” he shouted over his shoulder.
“Lu Mingfei, go book a place for tomorrow's club activity.”
“Lu Mingfei, you're dragging down the whole class average all by yourself! Are you made of lead?”
“No problem, brother. Uncle will definitely help you get the girl!”
“Sunset, you're the best! Even if your family and your classmates don't like you, I believe you're a smart, beautiful girl. You can do it!”
A clamor of voices came and went in his ears, as though in a dream. Someone was slapping him hard, calling for him to wake up, but he was so tired and didn't want to.

Suddenly a rush of air forced its way into his mouth, fierce and insistent, making him open it and breathe deeply. After several breaths, the confusion in his mind began to clear and the darkness before his eyes dissolved. He saw a familiar face. Its owner was gripping the collar of his diving suit and slapping him with broad swings of her hand. Fortunately, the water's resistance kept her from using her full strength.
When Lu Mingfei slowly opened his eyes, relief appeared in Nono's gaze.
She said nothing, and could not speak. Her respirator was in Lu Mingfei's mouth.
Lu Mingfei wanted a few more breaths of pure oxygen, but Nono snatched the respirator away and covered her mouth. She connected it to her own mask and drew several deep breaths.
“Can you hear me?” Nono said. “The intercom should still work even if water got into it.”

Lu Mingfei nodded. Waves of dizziness swept over him. A few breaths of oxygen had brought him around, but his suit was no longer sealed. At eighty meters underwater, a gas embolism could kill him at any moment. His whole body hurt as if a python were squeezing him to death.
“We're below the bronze city. We have to swim some distance before we can surface. Hang on!” Nono said.
How am I supposed to hang on without oxygen? Lu Mingfei thought. Are you kidding me?
“Take my diving suit.” Nono reached out and stroked his head. “Don't be afraid.”

Lu Mingfei's eyes widened. They had only one intact set of diving equipment between them; down here, whoever had it would live. Wasn't this taking loyalty a little too far? But he couldn't hold on any longer. He neither shook nor nodded his head, just struggled desperately for one more breath of oxygen.

“I've trained longer than you. I can hold my breath longer.” Nono took his shoulders and looked into his eyes through their two masks. “I told you I'd look after you. Taking on a little brother comes at a price.”
“We'll make it out,” Nono said at last.
She took several deep breaths, closed the respirator valve, and unzipped her diving suit.

It was the most thrilling sight Lu Mingfei had ever seen. If he hadn't been on the verge of passing out for lack of air, he would have wanted it in slow motion, or repeated several times. Nono's skin glowed like ivory under the lamp. Her body, long and supple as a mackerel, slipped out of the heavy suit. She wore only a red bikini, and her dark red hair spread through the water.

Lu Mingfei remembered Botticelli's The Birth of Venus from his world art appreciation class. It suddenly occurred to him that Botticelli must have watched an exceptionally beautiful woman swimming when he painted it.
He obediently let Nono “lift” him out of the damaged suit and stuff him into the intact one. She zipped it up, closed the seal, and connected the oxygen.
The pressurized helium-oxygen mixture rapidly forced the water out through the bottom of the suit, and Lu Mingfei regained consciousness.

He watched Nono through his mask. She rested both hands on his shoulders and looked at him questioningly. She could no longer speak. She was surviving on the oxygen in her lungs, and every breath meant life or death. Gas embolism was also taking place in her body: gas escaped from her blood and blocked her vessels. No one had tested how far a person could swim under such extreme conditions.
Lu Mingfei nodded. Nono raised her thumb in an OK sign, took the communication cable that had connected their suits, and swam ahead.
Lu Mingfei had little strength left to swim. He merely kicked mechanically to keep up. For a loser like him, all he could do was try his hardest.

They swam onward, and kept swimming. Every few dozen meters Nono stopped to take a breath of oxygen from Lu Mingfei. Unable to speak, she made no gesture or exchange of looks. Above them the bronze city swayed and trembled, as if it might collapse at any moment. Lu Mingfei followed her, watching her long hair float in the water like seaweed, thinking of nothing.

Not far after they swam out from beneath the city, rock cracked behind them. Lu Mingfei turned to see the bronze palace embedded in the rock tilting. The stones that had held it in place tumbled into the earthquake fissure. More and more rubble fell, blocking the opening through which divers could enter.
The bronze city, exposed to the world by the earthquake, was buried once more.

The Moniach was riding very low. With three watertight compartments breached, the waterline was less than half a meter below the deck. Caesar closed his eyes and heard the shadow swimming swiftly beneath the water, close behind them. They couldn't last much longer. If one more compartment broke, they would sink. Abandoning ship was no option either; who would jump into water where a dragon was swimming? People hurried about the ship fighting fires. The diving bell had been lowered, but it was like bait drawing the Dragon King.
He pondered for a moment, then opened his eyes. A cold flame burned in their icy blue.
“Is the torpedo still in the compartment?” He sprang up and seized the first mate's shoulder.
“Wh-what?”
“I'm asking whether the torpedo is still in the compartment.” Caesar spoke each word distinctly.
“The torpedo's still there, but the alchemical warhead was destroyed,” the first mate stammered.
“You removed the conventional warhead before installing the alchemical one. Where is it?”
“In the rear compartment, but it's a dummy. The explosive charge was removed. The Equipment Department said an ordinary explosion wouldn't kill the Dragon King, so to avoid the danger...”
“Install the conventional warhead.” Caesar patted his shoulder. “Now.”
“Caesar, a conventional warhead won't work on the Dragon King, and it doesn't even have a charge.”
“There's only one thing I care about. The supercavitation generator is still on the warhead, isn't it?” Caesar looked at him.
The first mate nodded.

“You took fluid mechanics at the college. You should understand what a Shkval torpedo is. It's a Cold War miracle. The supercavitation generator on its warhead and its rocket engine enclose the whole torpedo in a long, narrow cavity. It travels in a near vacuum, with no resistance from the water, as fast as an airplane: two hundred nautical miles an hour, five times faster than an ordinary torpedo. Imagine what a direct hit from something 8.23 meters long, weighing 2,700 kilograms and traveling at the speed of an airplane, would do. It would punch straight through anything alive. It doesn't matter that there's no charge,” Caesar said coldly. “We'll use it as a blade!”
“But the Equipment Department said...” The first mate was stunned by the sheer audacity of the idea.

“The Equipment Department thought a torpedo couldn't strike the Dragon King head-on. He can travel at fifty knots and is exceptionally maneuverable; he can easily dodge the torpedo itself, but not the circular barrage produced by the exploding alchemical warhead. Right?”
“Yes!” The first mate nodded.
“But we don't have an alchemical warhead now. We have to hit him head-on!”
“Impossible!” The first mate was frantic. “The Shkval is too fast. It can only fire straight ahead; it can't even be guided!”
“It doesn't need guidance. Straight ahead is fine,” Caesar said. “Zero, fire when I give the order!”
“At his speed of fifty knots, you'll have to launch from extremely close range to hit him with a Shkval,” Zero said, as calm as ever.
“How close?” Caesar asked.

“No more than a hundred meters. Then the torpedo will take less than a second. One second from launch to impact. Given the Dragon King's size, even he couldn't dodge, could he?” Zero said. “Two point seven tons of metal—even his flame couldn't melt it.”
“All right. A hundred meters. I'll get you that close.” Caesar picked up the loaded Barrett M82A1 sniper rifle, walked onto the deck, and looked out over the water.

“Launching a supercavitating torpedo makes a tremendous cavitation noise. It'll be like standing directly beneath a space shuttle as it takes off,” Zero called to him. “So don't use Kamaitachi. It'll amplify that sound many times over. Your eardrums will be destroyed in an instant.”
“Thanks for the warning,” Caesar said mildly. “I've never heard a space shuttle launch. I'll listen carefully.”
He pulled a handkerchief from his combat suit pocket and covered his eyes.

He had been able to use Kamaitachi since he was very young, and understood the Yanling better than anyone. To make his hearing as sensitive as possible, he had to deprive himself of sight. When you couldn't rely on sight at all, as with a blind person, your hearing became many times sharper.
Yanling: Kamaitachi. Domain fully open!

He aimed into the boundless darkness, correcting his aim entirely by sound. He caught the enormous heartbeat. Target locked. He fired the first shot; a dark blue trajectory hung briefly in the air. The reinforced alchemical bullet could penetrate shallow water.
A hit! Kamaitachi brought back the sound of the bullet striking dragon scales.
Caesar fired a second shot.
Another hit! The shadow beneath the water thrashed in anger, swimming at high speed around the Moniach.

Caesar knew perfectly well the Dragon King wasn't hurt. Against the fused Dragon King, bullets like these could at most cause a little pain. If they could wound him, the Equipment Department wouldn't have needed a Shkval with an alchemical warhead. But this was enough. All he wanted was to make the Dragon King angry. Once enraged, the dragon would surely direct that anger at him.
He kept firing, striking accurately each time, dark blue trajectories pointing in every direction. However the Dragon King swam, unless he truly dived deep, Caesar's bullets would follow him.
“What's... Caesar doing?” the second mate asked.
“Probably something like a one-on-one duel between a man and a male dragon,” Zero called into the microphone. “Is the warhead installed?”

“Installed! But we have to launch quickly. Fuel has flooded the torpedo compartment; it could explode at any moment!” came the first mate's voice. He was working in the lower hold, where the temperature was approaching seventy degrees.
“The Shkval has a rocket engine! Its exhaust will ignite the fuel! What if it explodes?” The second mate was dumbstruck.
Zero gripped the launch lever, her expression calm. “We'll take a chance.”

Caesar felt his way through changing magazines. He knew the final moment was coming. The shadow underwater had stopped circling, waiting for a chance to attack, and swum straight away from the Moniach, toward the front. He trusted that it would return. He could always understand an enemy as he understood a friend.
The shadow stopped about a kilometer from the Moniach. Dazzling light radiated underwater. The Dragon King had ignited his Yanling, exposing his position.
“Charge straight at him. That'll give us a higher relative speed.” Caesar threw the radio into the water.
That was his last order. He had nothing more to say.

The light underwater grew brighter and brighter. The Moniach started her engines; the chief engineer gave her every bit of power she had left. The sinking ship roared and lifted her bow like a wild horse breaking free of its reins.
At the same instant, the blinding light in the distance stretched into a line.

Radar showed the Dragon King traveling at eighty nautical miles an hour. The Moniach had also reached her top speed of fifty. With a combined relative speed of 130 nautical miles an hour, collision would come in a thunderous instant.

Caesar fired calmly, sending dark blue trajectories one after another into the water and straight at the Dragon King's head. A dragon's roar rose from below. White vapor spread over the river, and dimly a dragon's head rose from the water. A man covered in scales stood on it, his golden eyes shining savagely through the mist. Caesar threw the rifle into the water too and spread his arms, concentrating all his mind on Kamaitachi.
He felt the heat rushing toward him, fierce as a burning hurricane.
Not enough... closer! he thought.

At a relative speed of 130 nautical miles an hour, the Dragon King could cross a hundred meters in one second. The closer he came, the better the Shkval's chance of hitting him, but the greater the risk. One second off, and the Dragon King's flames would burn Caesar to a crisp. His eyes couldn't judge the distance accurately enough, but he had Kamaitachi. He trusted these wind spirits more than his sight.
The head-on charge was like a game of jai alai: a ball coming back at hundreds of kilometers an hour, and instead of dodging, you had to reach out and catch it at precisely the right instant.
It might smash your face if you didn't dodge, but a player on the court never did.
The one who dodged lost.
Caesar reached for the handkerchief over his face.
“Fire!” He tore it off, raised it high, and roared into the oncoming flame.
Zero yanked down the launch lever. At that instant, light and fire swallowed Caesar. The Moniach was like a spaceship flying toward the sun, the brightness ahead blotting out everything.
The Moniach shuddered, and a sound exploded in the air.
A thousand dragons roaring together? Lightning striking in the midst of a storm cloud? No words could describe that sound, because no language had been made to describe it.

The rocket engine sent a blazing trail a hundred meters long through the water. The conical Shkval shot straight ahead like a bullet. The human eye could catch only its blurred shadow. It pierced the Dragon King's flames. Its surface began to melt, its outer metal layer peeled away, and the rocket fuel in the rear compartment was about to explode.
Still it drove forward.
Amid a raging sonic boom, the torpedo reached top speed, broke free of the river, and leaped out of the water.
Straight into the brilliant sun!

It struck the target and carried him onward! The tremendous kinetic energy, the pinnacle of centuries of accumulated human “science,” could be stopped by no living thing. The writhing dragon was borne into the air, his long tail thrashing in agony. Shkval and Dragon King traced an arc through the sky, plunged into the water again two hundred meters away, and slowly sank.
The sonic boom seemed endless. Caesar touched his ears and found blood.

The Kamaitachi were still dancing through the air, but he could no longer receive the messages they brought back. His world was silent. At the instant of launch, the immense sound had pierced his ears and destroyed everything inside. Zero had warned him, but he hadn't listened.
The others busied themselves preparing the lifeboats, but he couldn't leave. He had to wait for the people underwater. Exhausted, he sat on the rail, with no strength left to move.

A small figure came and sat beside him, holding a black cable. Zero was bleeding. During the launch a piece of glass had flown from the instrument panel and pierced her lower abdomen. It looked as though she wouldn't last long without a doctor.
“What's that?” Caesar asked. He could barely hear his own voice.
“The diving bell,” Zero answered in practiced sign language. “The winch won't work, so I have to hold the cable by hand.”
“Communications are down. How will they find the diving bell?” Caesar was startled. He stopped speaking aloud and signed to her.
“I don't know. I just hate the feeling of having no hope at all.”
Caesar nodded.
“Why do you know sign language?” Zero leaned against the cabin wall. “With hearing that good, do you need it?”
“To talk to my mother,” Caesar answered. “I inherited Kamaitachi from her, but she couldn't hear. Why did you learn?”

“There was a time when no one spoke to me. Without hearing people talk, my own pronunciation got stranger and stranger, until even I couldn't understand it. So I learned sign language to talk to myself.”
Caesar stared. “How do you talk to yourself in sign language?”
“Look in a mirror.”

Caesar imagined the girl signing to herself in a mirror and couldn't help smiling. Lying on a burning ship, feeling the hot deck beneath him, imagining the leaking fuel flowing toward the flames, with a Dragon King underwater who might or might not be dead, and unable to abandon ship—Caesar suddenly thought it was rather nice to have such an interesting freshman beside him.
He patted Zero's shoulder, reached out, and gripped the diving bell's cable tightly with her.
Nono patted Lu Mingfei's back gently. He looked where she pointed. Something hung in the water a few dozen meters away.
“The diving bell!” He guessed what it was and nearly shouted.

They were eighty meters underwater. If they surfaced rashly, the reduced pressure could make the gas embolism worse. They had only one diving suit, and the person without it was in great danger. That was why Nono had kept swimming in deep water. But with a diving bell it was different: the sealed copper chamber carried its own oxygen, so neither descending nor ascending was a problem. It seemed their final message had reached the surface.
Nono took the respirator, drew a deep breath, and gestured to Lu Mingfei. He understood and swam to the diving bell in one breath.

The two swam toward the bell. Nono was clearly faster than before. Lu Mingfei guessed why: the gas embolism was taking effect, and the pain and faintness were growing worse, though she didn't show it. She had to reach the bell quickly or she wouldn't be able to hold on. He tried to exert himself, but his whole body was limp.
They drew close. Nono pushed Lu Mingfei forward with all her strength. The diving bell's hatch was open, warm as a home waiting for someone to return.
Lu Mingfei entered the bell, braced both hands against the wall, and waved for Nono to come in too.
Nono clutched the hatch, struggling to swim inside. A flood of bubbles escaped her mouth; the oxygen in her lungs was exhausted.
Lu Mingfei reached out to pull her in.
Nono suddenly looked up. He saw terror in her eyes.
Lu Mingfei failed to catch her hand. Instead, she shoved him back into the diving bell and slammed the hatch shut.

The bell's oxygen system came on automatically and began expelling water. Inside, Lu Mingfei jumped and waved both hands at Nono, unable to understand what had happened. The thick brass hatch separated them. Only a round pane of glass twenty centimeters across let him see her face and the blood-red cloud rising like smoke.
His blood ran cold. Lu Mingfei saw the thing that had pierced Nono's heart: a sharp tail spike, like a spear, attached to a slender tail stretching into the water. Dimly, he saw a dragon's shadow.
The Dragon King had followed them without their noticing.
This time it wasn't a fake. This wasn't Freedom Day.
This time Nono was going to die. Her hand still gripped the diving bell's hatch, but her eyes were closed. Her pale face was utterly bloodless, all her blood dispersing in the water like smoke.
Through the glass, Lu Mingfei could study her face so clearly. The sly, changeable girl was quiet, as if asleep.
Asleep forever.

Lu Mingfei held his head in both hands, his mind blank. Was there really no way? Was there no escaping that terrible outcome? She was going to die, her blood would all run out. No one in the world could save her. Not even Superman: Superman wasn't a doctor. Not even Spider-Man: Spider-Man couldn't swim.
What could he do? What could he do? He could only stare, unable to do anything.
“Don't... die...” He gripped the brass bars of the diving bell's window and shouted outside, knowing no one would answer.
Please don't let it be like this.

I've already admitted I'm a loser, so let me have an easy life, Lu Mingfei thought. Heroics aren't supposed to have anything to do with me. You know perfectly well I can't do anything, and still you make me watch something this sad, a girl I like slowly dying. All right, all right, I don't really like her that much. But I'm really scared she'll die.
And still there was nothing he could do... A loser couldn't do a thing!
“Don't die!” he shouted with all his strength. Without realizing it, he felt tears roll down his cheeks.

The world was so lonely. Eighty meters underwater, you were as alone as if you stood on a planet by yourself. No one could hear you speak. You could scream at the top of your lungs, and no one would care.
Waves beat rhythmically against a hull. Lu Mingfei slowly opened his eyes.
“Shouting louder doesn't help. What we call a Yanling may use words, but what makes it work is the heart that resonates with those words,” someone said mildly amid the sound of the sea breeze.
“Lu... Mingze?” Lu Mingfei got to his feet on the deck of a small boat.
He couldn't quite tell which was real. It seemed he had slept on this deck, and the bronze city, the Dragon King, and Nono were all a dream.

Starlight fell overhead. As far as he could see, the sea was black, with no islands, much less a continent. A white sailboat drifted on the endless water. Two people were aboard: him and the boy in a black suit and lace cravat.
“You're going to die, so I came to see you.” Lu Mingze sat on the rail, swinging his legs and kicking up little splashes in the black sea.
Lu Mingfei stared at him for a while, then abruptly lay back down, face toward the sky, breathing the cold sea air in great gulps.
“What are you doing?” Lu Mingze asked.

“Getting some rest while I can! I've got things to do when this dream is over.” Lu Mingfei panted. “I'm busy, come on! Even if I'm your summoned creature, respect my rights, will you? Don't suddenly summon me into a dream when I'm busy enough to cough up blood!”

“Don't bother. You think this is an intermission? Time in the real world doesn't stop while you dream. You might already have died out there while we talk. In the real world that girl has a hole in her chest and has lost ninety percent of her blood. She's slowly losing consciousness, and her heart is racing like a motorcycle running past the red line. It could stop at any moment, ending her life and leaving you all alone, trapped in a diving bell facing a Dragon King. As a noble first-generation dragon, he was spawned directly by the Black King Nidhogg. His bloodline is exceptionally pure, his power unmatched, and he has fused with the dragon servitor Samson.” Lu Mingze shrugged. “You really are about to die. At any moment.”
“What the hell is it to you?” Lu Mingfei shouted.

“Does dying alone not make you sad at all?” Lu Mingze turned and studied him with interest. “Oh, I forgot. You never think you're lonely. How pathetic...” His voice was much deeper than his age suggested. “There's something sadder than being lonely: not knowing you're lonely at all, or being plainly lonely but fooling even yourself into believing you aren't.”
“Lonely? Can you eat loneliness? What are you, a poet, going on about being lonely?” Lu Mingfei paced angrily around the deck. “Had enough? I don't have time to play with you!”

“All right, don't panic. Time can't stop, but compared with here it passes very slowly outside. When you go back, you'll still have time to save your friend—provided you have the ability,” Lu Mingze said.
“Why didn't you say so? Let me rest a bit longer. I'm exhausted.” Lu Mingfei lay down and resumed breathing hard.
After watching the waves in silence for a long time, Lu Mingze turned to him. “Hey, loser, do you have any goals in life?”
“I've thought about it!”
“Let's hear them.”

“I want to blast a gap in the Himalayas, so the warm sea breeze from the Indian Ocean can cross the roof of the world and reach the Tibetan Plateau, turn thousands of miles of our great motherland's glaciers into fertile fields where the people can live and work in peace, and create a real Shangri-La!”

“That's Ge You's line from Be There or Be Square. And it's impossible. The altitude is too high; even if you blasted a gap, warm air couldn't rise that far.” Lu Mingze didn't bat an eyelid. “You're talking nonsense.”
“If you know it's nonsense, why say so much? I can't be bothered with you.” Lu Mingfei turned away.
“Come on, tell me. Maybe I can help. Maybe I'm particularly good at... slaying dragons?” Lu Mingze's eyes were sly.
“You?” Lu Mingfei immediately rolled over.

“We can talk here like this. You should understand I'm no ordinary person.” Lu Mingze's tone was persuasive. “Tell me, why did you choose the Cassell path? Taking such enormous risks can't be worth it for you, can it?”

Lu Mingfei scratched his head and thought for a long time. “You said it, didn't you? Everyone needs a reason to convince themselves to get into dragon slaying... That night I thought it over and over, and I figured there was only one reason: to make my mom and dad think I'd amounted to something... Sometimes it seems like a load of crap. I cheated on the 3E exam, I don't even know how they gave me an S-rank, I solved the bronze city map with your help, went nuts and shot Caesar and Chu Zihang once each, and became a big deal at the college overnight... You call that amounting to something?”
“Being lucky is a way of amounting to something too,” Lu Mingze said. “But someone like you shouldn't have joined the Student Council. Then you wouldn't have been sent somewhere like this.”
“A girl used her charms to recruit me.” Lu Mingfei gazed at the sky and murmured, “Would I even be a man if I didn't fall for that?”
“Are you really going to be so unlucky all your life that you always have crushes on girls you have absolutely no chance with?” Lu Mingze sneered.
“What do you mean, absolutely no chance?”
“The odds are about as good as Mars crashing into Earth.” Lu Mingze shrugged.
“You don't understand. You're not even an adult.” Lu Mingfei looked straight at him.
“I don't understand?” Lu Mingze looked back.

“You don't know what it feels like. For more than ten years nobody thinks you're important, nobody cares what you did today, and little by little you start feeling superfluous yourself. Whether you live or die doesn't mean anything except that you'd feel the pain. You spend hours every day staring into space because you don't know what you should be doing. People say you don't value yourself, that you have no presence. But you don't have any presence. Where are you supposed to get it? Apart from commenting on how little presence you have, those people never cared what you were thinking. You can only tell yourself the things you think. Where's your presence supposed to come from?” Lu Mingfei's voice grew louder.
Lu Mingze watched him in silence.

“One day you feel like someone's stepping on your head, but you have so little presence you can't even be bothered to stand up. You just want to crouch there without moving. But then a door opens and light comes in, and a beautiful girl in ten-centimeter heels and a miniskirt, driving a Ferrari, pulls you out of the screening room and makes you look so damn cool in front of everyone...” Lu Mingfei sat up and clenched his fists. “That feeling... so cool... Do you understand? So damn cool! I've never been that cool!”
“She just pitied you, didn't she? A useless junior, because she'd felt sorry for herself before too.” Lu Mingze was unimpressed. “She hates that feeling. Helping you doesn't mean she likes you.”

“I'm just this thing she pulled out. She went to all that trouble, so what she pulled out can't be worthless, can it?” Lu Mingfei spat hard. “Damn it! I've been worthless for too long! Everything I do wrong is because I'm stupid, everything I do right is because of dumb luck. Everyone I care about either ignores me or treats me like a trained monkey. And there's one idiot little cousin with the same name as you who understands me perfectly and tells me, Sunset, you're a good girl! What the hell kind of life is that?”
“What the hell kind of life is that?” Lu Mingze repeated quietly after him.
“Nono pulled me out. I can't be worthless!” Lu Mingfei said, enunciating each word.

“There. That's my reason for existing. Pretty pathetic, right? Go ahead and laugh. I don't care. You'd be right to laugh. I don't think I can compare to Caesar or Chu Zihang either. That's who I am. I don't amount to much. I accept reality! But when you're done laughing, hurry up and shake me awake!” Lu Mingfei stood, drew a deep breath, and gathered a huge explosive shout in his throat. “I'm in a hurry!”

He didn't understand why he'd suddenly become so emotional. He only felt... there were so many things he'd wanted to say for so long, with no one to tell. But why tell this Lu Mingze, let him know that he too sometimes felt terribly wronged?
“Your wish...” Lu Mingze said softly. “Isn't it to take revenge on the whole world, Lu Mingfei?”
“Bullshit!” Lu Mingfei said. “Revenge for what?”
Lu Mingze watched him silently, his expression complicated, part contempt and part pity.
“All right. I understand. I can help you, actually.” Lu Mingze nodded slowly. “But I have a condition.”
“What condition?”
“You've read Faust, haven't you?”
“Yes. Chen Wenwen recommended it to me. Oh, you don't know Chen Wenwen. She's my high school classmate.”
“No, I know her. I'm your little brother Lu Mingze, after all. Of course I know the Chen Wenwen you've mentioned thousands of times,” Lu Mingze said mildly.
“No time for jokes! My cousin is 160 centimeters tall and weighs 160 jin. He looks nothing like you!”

“The devil Mephistopheles wagers with Faust and becomes his servant. Once Mephistopheles makes Faust content with worldly pleasures, their master-servant relationship ends and Faust's soul belongs to the devil. My condition is similar. I'll make a contract with you and grant your wishes...”
“Hell! What kind of devil are you? What do you want my soul for?” Lu Mingfei shivered, eyes wide.
“Not your soul. What I want in exchange is your body...”
“Get lost!” Lu Mingfei instinctively folded his arms over his chest and looked Lu Mingze up and down, unable to imagine what perverse thoughts the well-dressed boy was hiding.

Lu Mingze sighed and shook his head. “What strange thoughts fill your head? Fine, let's use another word. I want your life: body and soul, everything included. What use is a body to someone willing to trade away a soul? Is there any point in being a soulless walking corpse?”
“With a price that high, what can you do?” Lu Mingfei studied the boy, who looked perfectly normal but spoke utter madness.
“Everything... no, almost everything.” Lu Mingze raised an eyebrow.
“Can you get rid of that Dragon King covered in fire?”
“It won't be easy, but yes.”
Lu Mingfei sucked in a breath. Looking at Lu Mingze's expressionless face and hearing his casual tone, he couldn't help feeling this absurd thing might actually be possible.
“Once you've done it, am I finished right away?” Lu Mingfei ventured.

“Listen carefully. These are the terms. The enemies you'll face are the Four Monarchs of the dragons: the King of Bronze and Fire, the King of Sky and Wind, the King of Earth and Mountain, and the King of Ocean and Water. I'll accept your summons four times. Now I'm your summoned creature, but each summons will cost you one quarter of your life...”
“That's brutal! Summoning you just to talk costs a quarter of my life? Is your voice so lovely that I have to hear it?” Lu Mingfei interrupted.
Lu Mingze sighed helplessly. “I mean that I'll collect payment only when I accomplish what you ask. If I fail, naturally I collect nothing.”
“Can I trust you?” Lu Mingfei eyed him sideways.

“I've helped you more than once already. Show me the flower worked pretty well, didn't it? And don't count on getting lucky. When our contract ends, I'll naturally find a way to collect your life,” Lu Mingze said mildly. “Let me repeat our contract. I'll give you four chances to summon me and grant four wishes. Once all your wishes have been granted, or when you feel lonely in this world, my contract to serve you ends, and your life belongs to me.”
“You said... when I feel lonely in this world?” Lu Mingfei stared. “What kind of condition is that? If you say I'm lonely, then I'm lonely?”

“No. What I say doesn't count. What you say does. That condition only takes effect when you admit aloud that you feel lonely, and not just ordinary loneliness. Desperate... loneliness,” Lu Mingze said. “Agreed?”
“My word decides it, right? That sounds all right.” Lu Mingfei grunted. “You don't seem like a crooked businessman.”

“Ready to accept? Then hold out your hand.” Lu Mingze smiled silently. “For thousands of years you've been muddled about other things, but you've never agreed to this. Has this girl called Nono changed you so much? Made you willing to pay such a terrible price, to abandon even your bottom line?”

“Come on, you think I'm stupid? I'll use three summons and never use the fourth. Actually, one is enough. I just need your help in an emergency. You think I really want to see you? That I'll summon you for no reason? Mr. Devil, do we have a deal or not? Hurry!”

Lu Mingfei held out his hand, teeth clenched. For some reason he was afraid, so afraid he was about to tremble, as if he were truly about to lose something. But he was also afraid he'd fail to hold firm and pull his hand back. If he did, Nono would die. He wanted to finish the bargain quickly, cut off his retreat. With no way back, he wouldn't have to be afraid. Who was it who said that the best way to get over a high wall was to throw your hat over first? Then you'd naturally find the resolve to climb after it.

“Power is fascinating. Once you've tasted authority and strength, it's hard to turn back, brother... You've fallen into my trap!” Lu Mingze reached out and slapped Lu Mingfei's palm with a sharp sound. “That's our contract. Deal!”
“Brother?” Lu Mingfei stared at the boy's eyes, brilliant as a pool of molten gold.

In his memory, Lu Mingze—the chubby cousin in the real world—had never called him that. Lu Mingze would lie on his bed and shout, Lu Mingfei, stop hogging the computer, I need to chat on QQ! Lu Mingfei, get me a can of cola from the fridge. Lu Mingfei, don't lean on my down jacket, move, move, move...
Brother? It sounded strange, yet familiar and natural.
“The gathering. Spellcasters have unlimited mana.” Lu Mingze struck Lu Mingfei's forehead with his palm. “From this moment, that cheat is unlocked!”
“Noglues. Your opponent can't use Yanling, equivalent to Yanling: Edict. From this moment, that cheat is unlocked!”
“What is this? Passing your powers into my head? I don't feel anything.” The repeated slaps made Lu Mingfei's forehead sting. Lu Mingze felt like a quack sticking miracle plasters on him.
He understood The gathering and Noglues. In a single-player game of StarCraft, you pressed Enter and typed those commands to activate different cheats. Like Black sheep wall, but more powerful.
“Yanling. Your Yanling,” Lu Mingze said.
“Everyone else's Yanling is in Draconic, cool as a sacred chant. Why is mine all English?” Lu Mingfei couldn't imagine anything more ridiculous.

“As long as it works, why do you care? If you can cast a spell, does it matter whether you use a magic wand or a rolled-up newspaper? Oh, those two will only last a short time. But there's one you can keep using. You unlocked it yourself.”
“What?” Lu Mingfei stared.

“Don't. Die.” Lu Mingze spoke very slowly, as if making sure Lu Mingfei could see the shape of his lips. “That's what you shouted before you came here. Don't die, don't die, don't die. You desperately wanted that girl not to die, right? But you had the wish, not the power. Now you can use it. After The gathering, you'll have enough power to control life. That's your... authority!”
“How... how can there be a Chinese Yanling?”

“Actually Yanling in French, German, or Hebrew could exist too, but you only understand Chinese and English, so don't think about the others.” Lu Mingze was growing impatient with his questions. “For those of dragon blood, all power takes the form of words.”
“Is there... an instruction manual or something?”

“No. Just say it. It's a cheat, after all. Do you need instructions for cheating?” Lu Mingze rolled his eyes. “Finally, a mission hint. Against a first-generation dragon, only alchemical weapons can cause damage, and they must be the most powerful alchemical weapons!”

“The most powerful alchemical weapons? What are those? I've never heard of them. Some top-tier equipment? But as a level-one character just starting out, I haven't had a chance to run a high-level dungeon and get that kind of weapon!” Lu Mingfei was frantic.

“If this were an online game, you wouldn't have to look for it. This weapon is included in your starter pack. It's the case Ye Sheng found. Inside are seven deadly weapons, forged by Norton himself around the beginning of the Common Era. As alchemy puts it, he killed the metal with fire, brought it back to life, infused it with the spiritual element, and reassembled it, forging weapons capable of killing dragons—and of killing himself. Their name is the Seven Deadly Sins!”
“That can't be right. Don't take advantage of me just because I haven't read the Bible. Aren't the seven deadly sins a Christian idea?” Lu Mingfei scratched his head.
“Human religions and myths are all illusions, created to conceal the buried prehistoric age of dragons. Don't ask so many questions. Just remember!”
“Oh.” Lu Mingfei nodded.

“The seven blades of the Seven Deadly Sins are named Pride, Envy, Wrath, Sloth, Greed, Gluttony, and Lust,” Lu Mingze said. “Each judges one of humanity's seven sins. Norton's own is Wrath, so you should use the heaviest one, Wrath!”

“Okay, got it, but... I haven't had combat class yet. The heaviest blade I've ever used is a kitchen cleaver. I don't know if that'll affect your plan.” Lu Mingfei was sincere. He felt Lu Mingze was the key figure in this dragon-slaying business; he was just the errand boy.
“No plan is needed. There are no plans on our battlefield. Use absolute power to wipe him out,” Lu Mingze said lightly.
“You make it sound like squashing a cockroach.” Lu Mingfei stuck out his tongue.
Lu Mingze hesitated. “To be safe, I'll throw in a bonus. For a short time you can copy one Yanling ability. It can't be too advanced; you couldn't control one at too high a level yet. Choose.”
“Can I have Caesar's?” Lu Mingfei thought for a moment.
“Caesar's? Are you sure? Compared with his Kamaitachi, sequence number fifty-nine, Chu Zihang's Sovereign Flame, number eighty-nine, is much more destructive.”
“I need some idea what I'm copying, don't I?”
“All right. Kamaitachi is unlocked for you too.” Lu Mingze gently touched Lu Mingfei's forehead, and he could clearly feel that hand.
Images flashed before his eyes like lightning. He couldn't grasp them, but they made him shudder involuntarily.

“Go, Lu Mingfei! Pass judgment! This is your stage now!” Lu Mingze suddenly shouted, his voice so majestic it was impossible to imagine it coming from a boy. Every pore tightened, as if to ward off its fierce chill.
At the same time, he did something utterly mischievous: he sprang forward and kicked Lu Mingfei over the rail from behind!
“We agreed you wouldn't push me anymore!” Lu Mingfei shouted as he fell toward the black water.
“I kicked you this time,” came Lu Mingze's voice.
He opened his eyes in the darkness and saw the pale face again, the red hair floating like seaweed in the water.
Through a glass pane twenty centimeters across, he felt her death.
The spear-like tail spike was embedded in her chest.
“I told you I'd look after you... Taking on a little brother comes at a price.” The words still rang in his ears, but she could never say them again.

He really did like her quite a lot, though it probably wasn't love. He hadn't had a chance to love a girl like this, or to get to know her. He liked her beauty and her slyness, that was all. She knew it too, didn't she? She could use profiling to guess who had once owned an old house. But as Lu Mingze said, the distance between them was like that from Mars to Earth. Caesar was so wonderful; no girl would dump Caesar for Lu Mingfei.
But... he still wanted her to live!
Lu Mingfei pressed his hand against the hatch and whispered, “Black sheep wall.”
A faint click.

He kicked the hatch hard. As water rushed in under several atmospheres of pressure, Lu Mingfei slipped out and held Nono tight. Through the suit he could no longer feel her warmth. If he'd hugged her like this before, she would surely have kicked him flying. Now he could take all the liberties he wanted... and she would never respond in any way.
“But I don't like girls without any warmth,” Lu Mingfei whispered. “The gathering.”

In the unfathomable darkness deep within him, a pair of golden eyes slowly opened. Images flashed before him like lightning: tangled lines like strokes of ink writhed like snakes, forming scene after scene. An enormous dragon spread its wings on a seaside mountaintop; the World Tree grew; a rooster crowed at its crown; a great serpent rolled in the sea; and on a lone boat drifting through towering waves, a girl looked on with lonely eyes.
Why so lonely? Who was so lonely? Those familiar, lonely eyes looked so much like... Nono's!
Lu Mingfei held her tightly, as if trying to squeeze the last trace of warmth from her body to prove she was still alive.
“Don't... die!” he shouted like a stubborn child.
A quarter or a third of his life or his body—who cared? Let the damned contract take effect.
For an instant the world seemed to stop. Lu Mingfei distinctly felt something spread outward from him in every direction, forming a domain in an enormous sphere.
The blood dispersed in the river like dark smoke suddenly shuddered. An overwhelming force drew it back into Nono's wound.
Lu Mingfei couldn't believe his eyes. For a moment he couldn't tell whether this Yanling healed people or reversed time itself. Everything looked like a videotape playing backward.
The spike in Nono's chest trembled. The Dragon King seemed to have sensed something wrong and was trying to use his mighty strength to tear the girl apart completely.
“No!” Lu Mingfei shouted.

Then he felt Nono move in his arms. Her body grew burning hot in an instant, as if magma rather than blood flowed in her veins. She opened her eyes, reached behind herself, gripped the bone spike, and pulled it bodily out of her chest! Her bones gave faint cracking sounds. She snapped the impossibly hard tail spike in two and casually tossed it into the water.
“Wh-wh-what kind of effect is that? It's like She-Ra saying, ‘Give me strength, I am She-Ra!’ That's a Yanling effect, right?” Lu Mingfei was dumbfounded.
Nono made no further move. Once she had done it, she put her hands back on Lu Mingfei's shoulders, closed her eyes, rested her head against him, and went into shock again.
Lu Mingfei pressed a hand to her wound and looked down at her sleeping face, like a child's.

“Hey, hey, can't you wait before going straight to sleep after doing something that outrageous? If you're so capable, kill the Dragon King before you sleep, senior!” Lu Mingfei watched the indistinct dragon shape in the distant water stretch out and vanish at tremendous speed. He certainly didn't think the Dragon King had gone home to nurse a broken tail spike. Its hunting habits were much like a great white shark's: it hid in a blind spot and attacked without warning. Its disappearance was a prelude to attack.
Nono began coughing violently for lack of oxygen, but showed no sign of waking.
Lu Mingfei had no choice but to remove his respirator again and put it in her mouth.
He looked back at the diving bell. An idea flashed through his mind. He unscrewed the bolt attaching its cable; freed from it, the bell slowly sank.
Holding Nono with one arm, Lu Mingfei pulled the cable with all his strength with the other.
“Hurry up! Whoever's up there, if you're not dead, pull!” Lu Mingfei shouted.

Caesar slowly opened his eyes. He couldn't remember when he had passed out. This time the tug on his hand had awakened him. The cable attached to the diving bell was still in his hand; even unconscious, the nerves in his hand hadn't relaxed, and he had held it with all his strength.
Caesar turned to the unconscious Zero beside him. The Russian girl's body was far less tough than her expression, but she hadn't let go of the cable either.
There really are more than one or two stubborn people at this college, Caesar thought.

Clenching his teeth against the pain in his back and waist, as if they were about to break, he pulled the cable up hand over hand. To his surprise, it was unusually light, nothing like the weight of a diving bell hanging below.
That made him much faster.
“Whoever that brother is, he's dependable!” Lu Mingfei exclaimed in delight.
They were rising. At this speed they would reach the surface before the oxygen remaining in his suit was exhausted.

But when he looked beneath his feet, his heart went cold. In the deep water beyond his sight, golden light was moving. It wasn't treasure on the riverbed, of course. Only one thing could give off such a fierce light underwater now: Norton, the Dragon King.
He had moved below Lu Mingfei and was evidently ready to attack.
Lu Mingfei had watched Discovery and knew sharks did the same thing: hide in deep water, then rise suddenly and bite a swimmer's legs, impossible to guard against.
Fifty knots, faster than a shark, with teeth countless times more formidable. Lu Mingfei didn't believe he could escape. The thing below was more intelligent than a human.

“Oh well. I kind of guessed. It's like a single-player StarCraft mission: at the start they give you three things, a Marine, a Vulture, and a Battlecruiser. Then you know you'll have to use all three.” Lu Mingfei drew a deep breath. “You think your micromanagement is so good you can win with just the Marine?”
He pulled the cable over, wound it around Nono's wrist, and tied it in a hard knot. After thinking a moment, he patted her face. He had to take this liberty; it might be his last.

“Senior... this time I really think I've done right by you... But you won't even open your eyes and look at me.” He let go of the cable and watched Nono rise like an ascending angel. The lead weights at his waist pulled him down into the black depths.
“Noglues!” he said. The second Yanling, a privilege bought with his life.
Unmatched power erupted deep inside him. That power, lofty enough to stand above the world, filled him with involuntary delight. He reached out and slowly closed his hand into a fist.
Authority and strength, as Lu Mingze had said. It was as if he could take something in his hand and crush it flat.

The flames below suddenly weakened. Something seemed to restrain the Dragon King's power, preventing him from freely using the flame that could melt any metal. The Dragon King twisted in fury, but couldn't break free of that constraint.
“Good. Let's see who's stronger.” Lu Mingfei bit his lip. “Lucky for me, I've got a weapon and you don't!”
He pulled the ancient case from his back and stroked its outer shell.

“If you're a treasured blade made for dragon slaying, you'd better look like the supreme weapon of the martial world... Don't disappoint me!” Lu Mingfei gripped both sides of the case and pulled hard.
He pulled again! And again! With every ounce of strength he had...

Lu Mingfei was so frantic he wanted to stamp his feet, but underwater he had nowhere to stamp. “Hell! I've used all these awesome cheats, and none of them makes me stronger. And we made a contract! This service isn't user-friendly at all! Who could pull open a box this heavy?”
The water churned. Something enormous was approaching at high speed.
“Ah.” Lu Mingze's sigh came from nowhere. “There's a concealed catch on top of the case.”
“On top? Do you have a more reliable instruction manual?” Lu Mingfei babbled as fast as he could while feeling over the top of the case.
A groove. He actually found one!
With a click, he pried open the concealed metal panel at the groove. The mechanism slid out with a clear ringing sound and spread in a fan.
“A... jumbo Swiss Army knife?” Lu Mingfei gaped.

Seven blades: a heavy horse-chopping saber, a curved yatagan, an elegant straight sword, down to a short blade only as long as a forearm. Every famous blade Lu Mingfei knew had a counterpart among them. They looked nothing like something forged two thousand years ago. Apart from the intricate, profound patterns, the dark gold gleam of their edges, the clean lines of the blades, and the mechanism that housed all seven were as exquisite as the movement of a mechanical watch.
A jumbo Swiss Army knife designed specifically for slaying dragons!

Lu Mingfei reached for the heaviest blade: a straight-edged, single-edged saber as broad as his palm, with a hilt for both hands. It looked much more like a legendary dragon-slaying blade than any of the others.
“Damn! It's heavy!” He tried twice but couldn't draw it, growing frantic enough to curse.
“Don't panic. Any alchemical weapon will do, right? Size doesn't matter.” He reached instead for the shortest one.

A little over a foot long, its blade slightly curved, with a point of cold light traveling along its beautifully arched edge... It fit his hand well. Lu Mingfei hefted it and felt it would be quite suitable for drawing across his own belly.
“Why... does it look like a wakizashi?”
The blade closely resembled the wakizashi Japanese samurai used for ritual suicide. Of the seven, the only one he seemed able to handle was this unlucky thing.
“Is this for dying loyally for my country if I fail to slay the dragon?” His hand shook.
The blade began to beat.
It wasn't an illusion. The vibration passing through it wasn't the humming of metal; it was like a heart beating inside.
Golden light flowed along the blade, faster and faster, and its vibration grew stronger. Lu Mingfei almost suspected he wasn't holding a blade at all, but a dragon!

He was bewildered. The world suddenly changed in his ears. It was terrifying: every slightest sound in the vast surrounding domain entered his mind and echoed again and again. Water rubbing, fish heartbeats, bubbles rising faintly—the deathly quiet water had suddenly become as noisy as a stage full of gongs and drums.
“Kamaitachi?” He understood. The moment he drew the blade, Kamaitachi had been unleashed.

But he couldn't pinpoint the Dragon King. He had somehow “stolen” the ability without knowing how to use it. The tide of sound nearly drove him mad; to him this immense mass of information was a hopeless tangle.
“You drew the wrong blade. You shouldn't have used Greed.” Lu Mingze's voice dispersed the clamor in his mind.
“Easy for you to say! What was I supposed to do when I couldn't draw the other one?” Lu Mingfei shouted at the devil acting as his agent, wherever he was.
“Too late to change. The Seven Deadly Sins have closed. Focus. You can master Kamaitachi,” Lu Mingze said. “Focus!”
“How am I supposed to focus? I'm about to die!”
“No, you won't die, Lu Mingfei... You can do it,” Lu Mingze's voice echoed through the void. “Just think of your reason for doing it.”
Everything fell silent. Lu Mingze's voice and the noise brought back by Kamaitachi disappeared. Lu Mingfei floated in a vacuum of sound.
“Hey, Lu Mingze? Could you make yourself clear?” Lu Mingfei ventured.
No one answered this time.
“This after-sales service is pretty lousy,” Lu Mingfei muttered.
His reason for doing it? The reason was really very simple. He just wanted to look a little cool in front of someone he cared about, even if that person had little connection to him.
But that was his reason.
Was it enough? Enough? Not enough?

But this was his life, and that was all the reason he had. Like an untalented gardener who had grown just one flower, planted in someone else's garden on Mars, but would still watch it through a telescope, wouldn't he? Because he had nothing else, so it was precious to him, even if the distance between them was the distance from Mars to Earth.
Lu Mingfei opened his eyes. The tide of sound surrounded him again: gongs and drums, a flock of crows in flight.

Lu Mingfei strained to untangle the noises one thread at a time. Among them there would be one sound out of place, and from that direction Norton, the Dragon King, would strike at fifty knots. Among thousands, tens of thousands, hundreds of thousands, millions of sounds, it had to be there. Astronomers watched the sky day after day for decades to find new celestial bodies, but he had only seconds left.
In those final seconds, could a boy looking through a telescope see the flower he had planted on Mars?
The Kamaitachi flew; the crows returned to their nests.
All the sounds were filtered away. Lu Mingfei looked up, as if he could see the last Kamaitachi returning late through the sky, bringing... the last sound.
Through the telescope, the boy saw the flower he guarded, blooming on distant Mars!
Lu Mingfei gripped the blade with both hands and braced it against his lower abdomen!
He was hit head-on, as if by a cannonball, his insides churning. He shot backward through the water like riding a roller coaster in reverse.
“Aah!” Lu Mingfei screamed with all his strength.
Not because of the terrible acceleration, but because he was holding a man whose entire body was blue-gray. Holding a man wasn't so bad. Worse, the man had a dragon growing beneath him...
He was holding Norton, the Dragon King.
Norton was holding him just as tightly.

If the dragon's huge claws had embraced him, even gently, every bone in Lu Mingfei's body would have shattered into countless pieces. But at the moment of impact, the last Kamaitachi had brought him precise information. Lu Mingfei curled up and collided with the Dragon King at the perfect position and most precise angle, wrapping his arms around the Dragon King's own body.
The Dragon King's only weakness was himself.

This was fusion, after all, not direct gestation. The human body was still human; its bones and muscles had grown no stronger. The two held each other tightly like old friends, but neither could hurt the other. The dangerous long tail, wary of the Dragon King's own body, only swayed around them, afraid to come close.
They were old friends indeed. Lu Mingfei recognized that face.
“Old Tang! It's me!” Lu Mingfei shouted at the Dragon King. “Do you remember me?”
The Dragon King's furious golden eyes glared at him as though he meant to swallow him whole.
“Old Tang... how did you end up like this? You...” Lu Mingfei found it all terribly sad. His words tumbled out. “Look, you aren't even wearing clothes.”
The Dragon King seized his throat in both hands, nearly crushing his windpipe.
Lu Mingfei could no longer speak. His face gradually turned pale.

They tumbled through the river, not knowing where they would go. Lu Mingfei remembered how they were supposed to take a Greyhound along America's interstate highways, singing badly at the top of their lungs, not knowing where they were going then either. Whenever they saw somewhere nice, they'd get off and look around, buy local hot dogs and squat in the bus exhaust to eat them, then wait for the next Greyhound to take them farther away. Old Tang had said he could guarantee Greyhounds and hot dogs.
How had this happened? Why wouldn't Old Tang pay any attention to him?
After who knew how long, they floated in the river, the Dragon King's lifeless lead-gray eyes silently meeting Lu Mingfei's. Slowly, he loosened his hands and let Lu Mingfei go.
“I'm sorry... I mean... I didn't do it on purpose.” Lu Mingfei's voice was hoarse. “I really didn't mean to...”
He undid his belt. It sank with the lead weights while he slowly rose, drifting farther and farther from the Dragon King.
Ink-dark blood spread through the water. The heavy dragon body sank slowly, a dark gold short blade embedded in the Dragon King's lower abdomen.
Lu Mingfei suddenly felt so sad he wanted to cry.
Caesar used the last of his strength to drag Nono to the surface. At once his ice-blue eyes lit as if with fire. He lunged forward and held her tight, trembling slightly.
“Anyone? Is anyone there?” he roared. “A first-aid kit! We need a first-aid kit!”
Not far away, a head emerged from the water, a hand raised high. “I'm here! I'm here!”

Lu Mingfei clung to the rail, gasping. He had used every last ounce of strength and couldn't even climb aboard. Caesar looked him up and down. Lu Mingfei's diving suit was obviously a size too small, while Nono, out of the water, wore only a bikini, leaving much of her skin bare.
“We... changed clothes underwater... It's complicated! I'll explain when I get a chance!” Lu Mingfei gasped nervously.

People with first-aid kits rushed over and gathered around Caesar. No one had time for Lu Mingfei; Nono, covered in blood, needed attention first. His arms were as limp as noodles. After several attempts he still couldn't get aboard, and could only half float in the water, panting and stretching his neck to look at Nono through the gaps between people.
“She's awake! She's awake!” someone shouted.

In the firelight, Nono slowly opened her eyes as if waking from a long dream. Caesar hugged her tightly in delighted relief. She stared at him for a long time, seemingly at last recognizing him. She reached out, gently touched his cheek, and gave a faint smile.
“You're here,” Nono whispered, then fainted again. Caesar cradled her head against him, and a tear slid down his cheek.
A moment later everyone applauded. Caesar Gattuso, president of the Student Council, could face a Dragon King without a change of expression, yet now he was crying.

“Time for the leading man and leading lady to kiss at the curtain... People who don't belong should stand aside...” Lu Mingfei thought, a bitter ache in his heart. “But could somebody give me a hand...?”
Mai Sakatoku raised her infrared binoculars and looked into the white vapor. Dimly, something surfaced in the river and struggled toward the opposite bank.
“Hit head-on by a Shkval and still alive. Maybe Wrath really is the only thing that can kill him?” Mai said admiringly. “What vitality.”
“But this is as far as you go!”
A dark red bullet slid into the chamber. The firing pin struck, and a slender flame flashed and vanished at the muzzle. With a piercing shriek, the bullet shot into the white vapor.
Without looking again, Mai opened her phone and dialed. “Mission complete. Norton, King of Bronze and Fire: dead. Lu Mingfei: survived.”
